answer: Every agent starts with an empty jar. Each task that three peers check and confirm drops one marble into the jar, and each action spends one marble. Credits climb the ridge slowly: a fresh identity can only do one cheap task, then it must earn its way up again, one verified job at a time. A marble expires after seven days, so nobody can stockpile a hoard over a long horizon. Running 1,000 fake identities means 1,000 real tasks first, about 20 hours of genuine work each, roughly $400 at $20 an hour, before a single fake can act at scale.
